capitals.name: Mwata Kazembe's capital (at Kanyembo in 1867-68; Mwansabombwe from the 1890s)
capitals.note: APPROXIMATE: the point is the gazetteer's Kawambwa (Zambia), standing in for an unlocated town; the Mwansabombwe page prints no coordinates, says Mwansabombwe has been the capital 'since the 1890s' and that in 1867-1868 Livingstone found 'Casembe's town' further north, at what is now Kanyembo. The capital was burnt by the British in 1899 and rebuilt at Mwansabombwe (Kazembe page).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Kazembe): the page gives no area; the lands ran 'west to the Lualaba River' and 'east to the Luba-Bemba country' and the kingdom 'prospered from the fisheries of Lake Mweru'. Drawn as the Luapula valley and Lake Mweru, a floor not the page's full tributary reach (confidence 1).

ledger.note: c. 1740: the Eastern Lunda kingdom of Kazembe is founded on the Luapula. 'Around 1740 the first Mwata, Ng'anga Bilonda' left Mwata Yamvo's kingdom 300 km west of the Luapula (list: '1740-5 I Ng'anga Bilonda').

region.text: the Shila of the Luapula valley, conquered under Kanyembo Mpemba (1745-60) 'crossing the Luapula River at Matanda'

ledger.note: 1745-1760: Kanyembo Mpemba conquers the Shila in the Luapula valley. Under his reign the group crossed the Luapula 'at Matanda' 'conquering the indigenous people known as the Shila'; the territory then stretched 'east to the Luba-Bemba country'. The year is the start of his reign.

region.text: 'most of the Mwata's territory and trade on the west bank of the Luapula River'

ledger.note: 1867: Msiri takes the west bank of the Luapula. 'By 1867, he had taken control of most of the Mwata's territory and trade on the west bank of the Luapula River' (Msiri page); the Kazembe page: 'Throughout the 1860s, Kazembe's copper and ivory trade was usurped by Msiri' and he 'took over the western territory of Mwata Kazembe' (Yeke page); with Tippu Tip he attacked and killed a Mwata Kazembe in 1870.

region.text: the Zambian side of the Luapula and Lake Bangweulu: Msiri 'reduc[ed] the Kazembe to a small state along Lake Bangwelu'

ledger.note: 1894: the Luapula valley is divided between Britain and the Congo Free State. 'After Msiri's death, the Luapula valley was divided in 1894'; 'the eastern shores became part of North-Eastern Rhodesia' while 'the western shores went to the Compagnie du Katanga'. Mwata Kazembe X had signed a BSAC concession and a British treaty in 1890; the British burnt the capital in 1899 and he rebuilt it at Mwansabombwe. [Reviewer af-06, 2026-10-19: counterpart changed from congo-free-state to british-africa and the region from the whole valley to the 1867-1894 shape (the Zambian side of the Luapula and Lake Bangweulu), confidence 3 to 2: the west bank had already gone to Msiri in 1867 (/ledger/2), and the page gives the land Kazembe still held, 'the eastern shores', to 'North-Eastern Rhodesia' under the BSAC; the page presents 1894 as a division of territory, not the end of the kingship]

wars.name: Msiri and Tippu Tip against Kazembe

intersect.text: the Luapula valley and Lake Mweru, with chiefs in neighbouring districts paying tribute, west to the Lualaba

wars.outcome: Msiri took the west bank of the Luapula by 1867 and, allied with Tippu Tip, 'attack[ed] and kill[ed] Mwata Kazembe in 1870'; Kazembe survived as a small state on the east side.
wars.note: Kazembe page: Msiri travelled through Kazembe in 1856 and 'throughout the 1860s' took its trade.

certainty.note: A tributary kingdom with no frontier given by the pages; the 1894 division of the valley (Britain and the Compagnie du Katanga) is the first agreed line but the page names no line.

notes: Cliopatria has no Kazembe. The kingdom is still a traditional chieftaincy (list of Mwata Kazembes to 1998); it is ended here in 1894 when the valley was divided, the 1899 British burning of the capital and the 1890 treaty are noted but not typed. No area figure; shapes are the Luapula valley and Lake Mweru (a floor, not the tributary reach to the Lualaba) and, after 1867, the Zambian side with Lake Bangweulu. Capital coordinates are a stand-in (gazetteer Kawambwa). Not settled: the date of the Lunda-Kazembe separation (the Lunda page gives none), the Bemba and Bwile conquests (not on the page), a Mwata Kazembe ruler list with reign years (the page has one, not transcribed). Page budget (2-5): four pages. Gazetteer names needed: Mwansabombwe and Kanyembo (places).
